result:
Round 179 passed C, so the decision is **CONTINUE**. Round 180 is **DUX-R-5b-3b**, the last part of the one-colour rule (DUX-R-5); `current-task.md` is ready for A. No app source was touched, and `git status` in the store stays clean.

**Round 179 outcome (from `c-round-179.json`)**
- C passed it with no bugs, and both browser checks ran (`browserVerified` and `realVerified` are true). Root published rounds 178 and 179 together as `15189d5`, which is the baseline for round 180. I checked that the tree matches C's verified end tree.
- Only one sub-check could not run: the fake-Bearer 403 check, because the backend is unavailable in the cloud. It stays open evidence, not a failure.
- DUX-R-5b-3a is now მზადაა. C-R178-BADGE-SELECTOR, C-R177-G1-562 and GATE177-S5 are closed.
- C's three info notes are recorded. One of them (the stale lines in doc 147) is fixed in round 180.
- No Critical, High or Medium finding is open.

**Why DUX-R-5b-3b and not the regression round:** the last regression was 2026-10-24, so the next is due on or after 2026-10-27. Today is 2026-10-26, so it is not due yet. The next round is expected to be the regression round.

**What round 180 changes**
- **Drag previews (ghosts):** the Library drop preview and the clip-move preview become a light neutral when the drop is allowed and grey when it is blocked. Today both states are the same brass, because in the Obsidian theme the two brass colours are identical.
- **File drag over a lane:** the outline goes light on the video lane and grey on an audio lane. The drop hint text is light in both cases.
- **Video import buttons (full and compact) and the Library Preview "Add" button:** they keep a visible border, in the neutral `outline-strong` colour, with light text.
- **Contrast:** I computed every pair and all pass. Allowed vs blocked differ by 2.21:1, the same step as Mute vs Solo.
- **Files A may change:** the 2 components, the 3 tests that check those colours, and doc 147. A also creates a new test file (DXG1–DXG7) and doc 148. The other 997 files are frozen.
- **Targeted tests:** I ran the 13 related test files on the start tree and got 242/242. A also has 8 mutations to prove the new tests catch colour regressions.
- **What C checks in the browser:** real drags at both window sizes; a file drag simulated inside the browser, since headless Chromium can't drag a real file; colours, brass pixels and contrast; and that dropping and moving still behave the same.
- **End-of-stage inventory:** C greps every remaining brass class in the Studio components. Each one must be selection, a playhead, the primary Export button, focus or an edit field, the preview playback fill, or the envelope. I named the Ruler playhead handle (l.233) and the Export dialog's primary button (l.615) in that list so they aren't flagged by mistake.

**Decisions for you (you can veto any of them)**
- **Allowed vs blocked drag colour:** blocked uses grey, not the theme's warning or destructive red. Both of those fail the brass-pixel check.
- **Refused file-drop hint:** the text stays light, because it is the only message the user sees when the drop is refused.
- **Import and Add buttons:** they keep a visible neutral border. The existing tests require a border, so a borderless style wasn't an option.

**If C passes round 180:** DUX-R-5 is complete. I will then ask root for a bounded frontend-architect review, with the shared-test-setup proposal from the last two code reviews as its main input, before M1. That proposal is recorded but not scheduled.

**Ableton parity:** unverified. I didn't open any Live 12 manual section or video about the colour of drag feedback or of add/import buttons. Drag and drop behaviour doesn't change, so there is no behaviour claim.

The advisor was available. I consulted it before writing and again at the end, and applied its four corrections to the task.
